big_case_rationale: Post-Jarkesy test of Article III limits on agency adjudication across federal benefit/immigration programs; SG petition, invalidated application of a federal statute, and 20+ merits amici from the Chamber, AFL-CIO, and the conservative legal movement.

semantic_claims.proposition: The majority will hold that DOL's H-2A enforcement action was in substance a common-law claim seeking legal remedies - civil penalties plus back wages that function as contract damages for breach of the job order's terms - so under SEC v. Jarkesy's private-rights presumption it belongs in an Article III court, and the immigration public-rights line (Oceanic Steam Navigation v. Stranahan, Lloyd Sabaudo v. Elting) will be confined to exactions tied to the admission and exclusion of aliens rather than extended to adjudication of an employer's domestic employment-law obligations.

The majority's stated ground will be narrow rather than categorical: limited to agency adjudication of contract-like monetary remedies (back wages and civil money penalties for job-order violations) with conclusive effect, expressly preserving administrative adjudication of admission, exclusion, and immigration-status matters and declining to announce any general rule against penalty adjudication within federal benefit or immigration programs.
